title: Post-optimization latency spike after enabling mixed-quant + aggressive KV prefetch — need safe rollback plan
content:
description:
Issue summary: After HealthNow applied the mixed-quant profile (mix-v2) with an aggressive KV prefetch policy and higher batching window, production request P50/P95 latency increased by ~3-6x. Impact: user-facing slowdowns for real-time document summarization flows; elevated error budgets for dedicated capacity pool. Environment: dedicated cluster in us-east, serving model gpt-like-13b-quant-mix-v2. Steps to reproduce: 1) Deploy optimizer profile 'mix-v2' + kv_prefetch: aggressive on tenant HealthNow; 2) Send typical 0.9s median prompt workload with streaming enabled; 3) Observe endpoint latency metrics and per-token time. Observed behavior: sudden increase in tail latency and increased variance on streaming chunk emission. CPU on CPU-side orchestrator spiked briefly; GPU utilization appears lower than baseline. Expected behavior: batching and prefetch should reduce per-token latency/cost without increasing tails. Investigation summary: Initial hypothesis is that KV prefetch combined with mixed quant causes memory thrashing on GPU and increased host-side scheduling delays due to longer prep time for larger batches. We see elevated host-side serialize/deser times in traces and repeated small fallback to full-precision kernel for certain attention sizes. HealthNow reports no model code change other than optimizer profile toggle. Temporary workaround applied: Disabled kv_prefetch for tenant; reverted batching window to baseline (25ms) which reduced P95 back to near baseline. Work needed: define safe, staged rollback that preserves throughput while minimizing cost and quality regressions; identify precise kernel/attention sizes triggering fallback. Attachments: dashboard links and sample trace IDs are in comments.

comments:
2026-03-13 09:18 - Aisha Patel: Created ticket after HealthNow CS escalated. Customer applied optimizer change yesterday evening and saw degradations at 23:30 UTC. They provided sample trace IDs and a short flamegraph from their observability snapshot.
2026-03-13 10:04 - Support Engineer (Miguel Torres): Confirmed P95 spike on Redwood Console for tenant healthnow-prod (dashboard: /dashboards/tenant/healthnow-prod/optimizer-metrics). Noted repeated host-side serialize spikes and a small number of 5xx retries correlating with the latency spikes.
2026-03-13 12:30 - SRE (Priya Menon): Looked at node metrics in us-east cluster. GPU memory fragmentation visible on a subset of pods running mixed-quant kernels. Observed OOM-kernel fallbacks logged in runtime: 'kernel_fallback=attention_full_precision' in /var/log/serving/runtime.log. Suspect mismatch between quant kernel selector and current attention length distribution.
2026-03-13 14:02 - Eng (Luca Bianchi): Reproduced locally with a traffic replay. When kv_prefetch is enabled aggressively plus batch_window >= 80ms, the runtime groups longer-context requests into mixed batches causing kernel selector to choose a safer (but slower) path. Proposed staged rollback: 1) disable kv_prefetch globally for tenant, 2) force batch_window to baseline, 3) pin model to pre-change variant for 48h while gathering perf traces.
2026-03-13 15:10 - Customer (HealthNow - infra@healthnow.com): Confirmed that disabling kv_prefetch and reducing batch window restored acceptable P95 within 10 minutes. Asked for a documented rollback checklist because they run hourly config syncs and want an automated safe-off ramp.
2026-03-14 08:21 - Support (Miguel Torres): Drafted rollback checklist below and requested SRE safety review. Also flagged potential follow-up: kernel selector telemetry missing for a small number of hosts; we need a bug ticket to add more granular kernel decision logs (INT-XXXX).

resolution_notes:
Workaround: kv_prefetch disabled and batch_window restored to 25ms for HealthNow tenant. Next steps: 1) Execute staged rollback playbook: A) snapshot current optimizer settings, B) disable kv_prefetch, C) set batch_window to baseline, D) pin model to gpt-like-13b:v2026-03-10, E) monitor on P95, P99 and error rate for 2 hours; 2) SRE to collect per-host kernel selector traces for the affected pods and upload to artifact storage; 3) Engineering to reproduce failure case in CI with mixed-quant + prefetch + larger batch windows and open a bug for kernel selector fallback (linked INT ticket will be created). Customer notified and accepted temporary mitigation. Follow-up: schedule a guided tuning session with HealthNow next week to test incremental optimizer flags with slower ramp and observability hooks.

notes:
Runbook reference: confluence runbook 'optimizer-rollback-guidance' section 'staged-offramps'
Priority is to reduce customer impact; cost regressions are secondary for initial rollback
Recommend adding automated guardrail that prevents enabling aggressive kv_prefetch when batch_window > 50ms for mixed-quant profiles
